title: Atomic Dashboard + Trace minimal slice and acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
The Console Observability initiative was scoped too broadly for the Q2 MVP. This ticket narrows the visible surface to an atomic deck that still provides actionable routing/cost/tracing signals while deferring heavy-weight features to later phases. The goal is a tightly-scoped, delightfully fast MVP for early customers and internal dogfooding.

What we're keeping for MVP (atomic slice):
- Three summary cards per route: request rate, 95p latency, estimated cost per 1k requests (aggregated). No per-token line items.
- Route-level trace sampling (1% by default) with a single-span waterfall view and error annotations. No distributed flamegraphs in MVP.
- Lightweight rollup for route capacity (requests/min, active GPU workers) for Dedicated customers.
- Cost explorer: route-level deltas and trend sparkline for last 7 days. No deep breakdown by kernel or quantization.
- API for export (CSV) of aggregated route metrics for accountants.

What we're cutting/defering from initial PRD:
- Per-token cost breakdown and token-by-token latency waterfall (defer to phase 2).
- Full-fidelity tracing capture (all spans + flamegraphs) — keep sampling and single-span view for now.
- Cross-route attribution and user-level cost tagging (defer).
- Long-term raw telemetry retention and heavyweight query capabilities (defer to telemetry-tier work).

Rationale and trade-offs:
- Prioritizing low-latency client UX and small telemetry ingestion footprint to hit SLA for the hosted console endpoints.
- Per-token + full trace retention increases ingestion and storage costs disproportionately for initial users; deferring preserves cycle and reduces infra risk.
- Maintaining parity of the core developer experience: minimal metrics for debugging + cost signals to enable release decisions and quick ops triage.

Acceptance criteria (must be met to mark Done):
1) Deck loads within 300ms median and under 700ms 95th on staging with production-like dataset (30 routes, 10k req/min synthetic).
2) Three summary cards render for any route with accurate numbers (validated against telemetry-backend within 2% for rate and cost estimates).
3) Trace sampling toggles work in Console and sampled traces link to full trace viewer (when available) or show inline waterfall with spans & annotations.
4) Cost sparklines show correct 7-day trend; export CSV produces route-level daily aggregates for requested date range.
5) UI feature flags exist to toggle per-token and flamegraph surfaces (default: off).
6) Instrumentation includes an event to capture "console.view.route.summary" and "console.export.cost.csv" for usage tracking.
7) E2E smoke test verifies traffic, trace sampling, and CSV export in CI.
8) Documentation (PRD update + brief runbook) and internal release notes completed before release.

Design and PM decisions made:
- Keep cards intentionally minimal to reduce cognitive load for first-time enterprise users.
- Cost estimate algorithm: use token-averaged unit-cost model (fast, lower precision) for MVP; attach note in UI about precision and upcoming improvements.
- Tracing: sampling-first approach; allow power users (admin role) to increase sampling on-demand per-route.

Acceptance test plan (high level):
- Run synthetic load job (scripts/test/console_mvp_load.py) to produce 30 routes at 10k req/min for 1 hour; verify card latencies and correctness.
- Toggle sampling to 5% for a test route and verify new traces appear in sampling bucket.
- Execute CSV export for 7-day window and assert row counts match aggregated telemetry queries.
- Manual UX review: design signoff on card spacing, labels, and explanatory tooltip for cost-estimates.

Release and rollback notes:
- Feature-flag all surfaces; ship behind "observability_mvp_v1" remote flag.
- Canary 10% of accounts for 48h, monitor error budget and latency.
- Rolling rollback plan: disable feature flag and revert frontend toggle if error budget breach >2% in 24h.

Open questions:
- Should Dedicated customers have higher default sampling? (proposal: yes, 2% for Dedicated).
- Finalize token-averaged cost constants with Finance by 2026-03-15.
